java_locations.role: Selects createNew for the first unordered endpoint pair, createSecondAssociation plus createInSecond for the second, and rejects a third association on the same pair.
Shares the original base-link model with the second point and, for a one-rank base, changes the first split pair to length two while keeping the first role connector at length one.

Creates a length-two second split pair, removes/inverts/re-adds the first point-to-role connector when necessary, adds the second point-to-role connector, then adds an invisible length-one edge from the first point to the second.
Projects the resulting mutable live-link list with stable unordered endpoint-pair grouping; reinsertion and the invisible constraint therefore affect serialization and layout.

rust_locations.role: Stores each association independently and has no first/second pair relation or shared base-link lifecycle.
Removes the latest A-B relationship for every association statement and appends an independent AssociationClass, rather than selecting Java's second-association path.
Always synthesizes three createNew-style links per point and cannot represent first-link reinsertion, changed first lengths, the second point connector, or the invisible point-to-point edge.

claimed_invariant: At most two association classes may attach to an unordered endpoint pair. The second statement is a transaction over both points and the shared original base: it mutates the first association's link lengths, may invert and reinsert its role connector, creates a length-two second split pair and a length-one second role connector, and adds an invisible first-point-to-second-point rank constraint. Live-link construction order after those mutations, not three independent links per statement, determines SVEK serialization and layout.
causal_divergence: Rust treats the second statement as another createNew. It removes no first split link because those links exist only as renderer projections, retains the first point-to-role orientation/order, emits another independent three-link set, and has no invisible point-to-point constraint. This changes both link identities/order and Graphviz topology in checker2_multiple_associations_same_pair. The single-association controls pass because Java never enters createSecondAssociation/createInSecond for them.
planned_model_change: Represent whether an AssociationClass is the first or second point for an unordered endpoint pair and retain the shared base/first association index. Parse the second statement without independently consuming a new base relationship; reject a third as Java does. Project the complete post-transaction live-link model: update first split lengths when required, invert and reinsert the first role connector when Java does, emit the second length-two split pair and length-one role connector, and include the invisible first-point-to-second-point edge in layout while suppressing its SVG paint. Derive UID consumption and SVG IDs from the same constructor/inversion sequence. Do not alter single-association geometry or generic relationship ordering.
perturbation_axes: pre-existing base length one versus length two versus no explicit base
second statement endpoint order same as versus reversed from the first
root ownership versus same-package ownership versus cross-parent statement ownership
second association followed by a third attempted association
acceptance: An independent checker creates fresh valid inputs crossing at least two listed axes and preserves every source, Java SVG, Rust SVG, command result, and diff under test-diagrams/perturbations/class-association-second-link-lifecycle/.
Every fresh Java-success input is byte-exact through diff_one --no-oracle; any nonzero fresh diff rejects the change.

The preserved checker2_multiple_associations_same_pair counterexample becomes exact through the modeled lifecycle, with the first connector orientation/order and invisible rank constraint matching Java.
Fresh one-association controls remain exact and a fresh third-association case matches Java's rejection/consumption behavior without fixture-specific branches.
Parser, renderer, perturbation, baseline-ratchet, and harness-guard tests pass at the reviewed implementation revision.
forbidden_approaches: branches keyed to fixture names, labels, pair counts from the golden corpus, source lines, or expected pass counts
coordinate offsets, per-branch-count layout constants, SVG post-processing, or golden/oracle reads from shipping crates
modeling the invisible edge as a painted SVG relationship or omitting it from layout because it is not painted
changing generic Graphviz constants, relationship ordering, comparator slack, baselines, park lists, error markers, or allow-lists inside this mechanism
